rules.yaml.heading: Worked example
rules.yaml.text: The State has 10 Resources. Şırnak (Mountain) holds 4 Troops, 1 Police, 2 Guards and 2 Underground Guerrillas. The State chooses Op + SA: Sweep in Şırnak (2 Resources). It Activates (4 + 1 + 2) / 2 = 3, round down, so both Guerrillas flip Active. As its SA it takes Air Mobility and moves 2 more Troops into Botan. It cannot Assault on the same action, because Sweep was its Op. Next card the PKK is First Eligible (CT 2.3.5). The PKK may March the Active Guerrillas out, or Rally to flip them Underground without a PKK Base. Coverage and tempo compete, as in CT lessons example 1.

rules.yaml.heading: Tests
rules.yaml.text:
1. Atrocity test (Claude harm file, section 6): for Village Clearance, Covert Action and Strike Collaborators, compute the net score change for the user at the next victory check. 09, section 7 gives the arithmetic. Any of these with a positive net score effect fails. Coerce is intimidation, not killing. It may shift a score (DD-06.5; CT 3.3.4) but its markers count toward the PKK Harm gate. 09, section 7 checks that bound.
2. Check that Cross-Border cannot end the game by itself. Count PKK Bases rebuilt in the KDP Zone within one Campaign.
3. Check Diplomacy odds. If a posture moves more than twice per Campaign by Diplomacy, raise the target to 6.

rules.yaml.heading: Principle
rules.yaml.text: Control, Support and Legitimacy are separate (DD-06; M-004). Control comes from pieces. Support and Opposition are per space. Legitimacy is national. No operation turns Control into Support. Support and Opposition abstract active minorities and mixed attitudes. They do not measure ethnic preference (CT playbook pp.13-14; F-034; F-049).

rules.yaml.heading: Levels and shifts
rules.yaml.text:
Each populated domestic space is at Active Support, Passive Support, Neutral, Passive Opposition or Active Opposition (04, section 4.1). A shift moves one level. Blocks:

1. A Coercion marker blocks all shifts in its space until it is removed.
2. A State Harm marker blocks shifts toward Support in its space.
3. A PKK Harm marker blocks shifts toward Opposition in its space.
4. An Office caps its space at Passive Support and at Passive Opposition (DD-18.4). The cap stops shifts beyond these levels. The procedure table never places an Office in a space at an Active level (section 6.4, line 4). The legal party is an independent alternative that neither armed side owns (DD-10.5).
5. Coerce and Strike Collaborators never shift a space toward Opposition (DD-06.5).

rules.yaml.heading: Civic Action and Agitation procedures
rules.yaml.text:
Civic Action (State). Used in Train (one space) and in the Propaganda phase (any number of spaces, total spending at most half of Legitimacy, round down [tune]; halved after the desk test in 11, IR-02). The space needs State Control and at least one Police (DD-06.4). In the Propaganda phase it also needs at least one Troop, as CT 6.3.1 requires Troops and Police [tune]. Reason: fidelity to CT 6.3.1. It does not by itself fix the State scoring pace found in the Stage 0 desk test (11, section 1). Costs, in any order the State chooses, except that a shift needs the blocks removed first:

| Step | Cost |
|---|---|
| Remove one Coercion marker | 1 |
| Relief: remove one Reception marker | 1 |
| Redress: remove one State Harm marker | 3 |
| Return: remove one Displacement marker (section 3.3) | 3 |
| Shift one level toward Support (maximum 2 shifts per space per phase or action) | 2 |

Agitation (PKK). Used in Rally (one space with a PKK Base or PKK Control) and in the Propaganda phase (spaces with a PKK piece and no State Control). In a space with an Office, Agitation may not shift the space beyond Passive Opposition (DD-18.4).

| Step | Cost |
|---|---|
| Remove one Coercion marker | 1 |
| Redress: remove one PKK Harm marker | 2 |
| Shift one level toward Opposition (maximum 2 shifts per space per phase or action) | 1 |

Evidence: pacification needs capacity and spending, and spending must not buy consent by itself (CT lessons table). Adapts CT 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 6.3.1 and 6.3.2. The cost gap (State 2, PKK 1) follows CT.

rules.yaml.heading: Legitimacy
rules.yaml.text:
One national track, 0 to 20 (DD-06.3).

| Change | When | Amount | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Emergency Rule drain | Propaganda | Martial Law -1, OHAL -1, OHAL Extended Powers -2, Normalizing 0 | F-013; F-055; M-010 |
| Village Clearance | At once | -2 x Pop | F-050; M-005 |
| Village Clearance late cost | Next Propaganda | -1 per New Displacement marker | F-050; F-043 |
| Village Clearance in a space with an Office | At once | -1 | DD-10.5 |
| Covert marker revealed | On reveal | -2 | F-028; F-030; M-009 |
| Reception markers 3 or more | Propaganda | -1 | M-018; F-032 |
| Disputed Harm markers 3 or more | Propaganda | -1 | F-029; F-058 |
| Europe at 4 or 5 | Propaganda | -1 | F-042; M-024 |
| Party ban | Legal Politics | -2 | F-015; F-017; M-007 |
| State breaks Reciprocal Restraint | At once | -2 | F-039 |
| Step Normalizing to OHAL | Propaganda | -1 | F-055 |
| Open Legal Space and 2+ Offices | Propaganda | +1 | F-052 |
| Reciprocal Restraint kept by the State | Propaganda | +1 | F-039 |
| No New Displacement marker flipped this round | Propaganda | +1 | Claude restraint step |
| Events | Card | As printed | F-042; F-043; M-024; M-025 |

Legitimacy feeds the State score, State income and the Civic Action cap. It is the main brake on State coercion. Court and EU effects come by event and arrive late, as in history [F-043; E-0211; M-025].

rules.yaml.heading: Harm markers
rules.yaml.text:
1. A Harm marker records civilian harm in a space. Its side names the State, the PKK or "Disputed" (DD-07.1).
2. Sources: Village Clearance (State), revealed Covert marker (State), Strike Collaborators (PKK), Cross-Border Assault (Disputed, zone only), events (as printed; Disputed when attribution is contested).
3. A Harm marker stays until Redress or an event removes it. It never leaves by itself.
4. Equal costs do not claim equal acts (DD-15.3). Card text prints the evidence level.
5. Harm markers in external boxes count for the Harm count but do not block shifts (boxes have no Support).

rules.yaml.heading: Displacement and Reception
rules.yaml.text:
1. Village Clearance places one Displacement marker (New side) in the cleared space and one Reception marker in Diyarbakır City, Van City, Batman City or Western Cities (06, section 3.4).
2. Displacement never lowers Pop for victory (DD-07.3). The CT Resettle Pop 0 rule is rejected (CT 4.2.1; CT lessons).
3. While a Displacement marker is present: the PKK cannot Rally, Extort or Coerce in the space. That is the State's gain: cut logistics [F-050; F-031].
4. The displaced space stays an obligation. It keeps the level that Village Clearance left (one level toward Neutral, DD-18.3) and scores at that level.
5. A Reception marker is a receiving-city obligation. The State must pay relief (1 each) before it can shift that space toward Support. Reception never places a PKK piece or an Office (Sol political systems file; M-018).
6. No victory condition counts displacement as a positive (DD-07.4).

rules.yaml.heading: Return
rules.yaml.text: Return removes one Displacement marker for 3 Resources by Civic Action. It is legal only in C5, at Normalizing, or by a Return event [E-0136]. It never removes the Harm marker in the space and gives no Support. Return was small in history: 26,481 returnees by end 1999 per government figures [Q-281]. Displacement totals stay contested [F-032].

rules.yaml.heading: Village Guards (DD-08)
rules.yaml.text:
1. Guards enter play only after the Law 3175 event [E-0004; E-0005; F-010].
2. Placement: Train in a Mountain or Plain space with State Control and Police (06, section 2.1).
3. A Guard stays in its home space. It counts for Control there. It never moves by Sweep, Air Mobility, Garrison or Redeploy (DD-08.2).
4. Guards add to Sweep and Garrison activation in their space (local knowledge). They do not add to Assault.
5. Upkeep: 1 Resource per 2 Guards each Propaganda round (DD-08.3) [Q-347].
6. Removal: PKK Attack (after Troops and Police), Strike Collaborators (with a PKK Harm marker), upkeep failure, events. A removed Guard never becomes a PKK piece (DD-08.4).
7. Guard Abuse events: when such a card is executed, in every space where a Guard shares a space with any Harm marker, Legitimacy -1 and remove one Guard there, once per qualifying space (DEC-57). Card text says "some guards", not a share [F-012; Q-193 is Low].
8. Guards have no victory score and no independent aim [F-057].

rules.yaml.heading: Posture effects
rules.yaml.text:
| Posture | PKK Rally in the box | PKK March into the box | PKK income per Base in the box | State Cross-Border |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Host | Guerrillas or Bases | Normal | +1 | Not allowed |
| Tolerant | Guerrillas only (KDP and PUK: Bases too after Northern Iraq Vacuum) | Normal | +1 | Not allowed (allowed after Northern Iraq Vacuum) |
| Restricted | None | +1 Resource; group Activates | 0 | Allowed (KDP and PUK) |
| Hostile | None | Not allowed. Guerrillas in the box are Active, except that Reset flips them Underground (prototype DEC-53) | 0 | Allowed (KDP and PUK) |
| Aligned with Turkey (KDP, PUK) | None | Not allowed. Guerrillas Active, except that Reset flips them Underground (prototype DEC-53) | 0 | Allowed, no extra cost; no Mountain modifier for Assault |

Syria-Bekaa never allows Cross-Border. The C1 and C2 hot pursuit exception for the KDP Zone is in 06, section 3.2.

rules.yaml.heading: Rules
rules.yaml.text:
1. Each posture moves on its own. Closing one never moves another (DD-09.1).
2. Moves: State Diplomacy (06, section 3.3), PKK Host Pressure (06, section 5.4), events, State Pivotal "Coercive Diplomacy on Syria". No automatic reset (DD-09.4; ADP 6.6.1 reset rejected).
3. A posture change never removes pieces. It suspends Rally and income (DD-09.5).
4. Leadership: the marker sits in Syria-Bekaa on its Present side. When Syria reaches Hostile, flip it to Abroad. While Abroad it gives no income and Host Pressure on Syria is not allowed. Capture is an event effect only, on the mandatory C5 Capture card, and applies only if the Leadership is Abroad (DD-09.6) [E-0018; E-0130; E-0020; F-021].
5. After Capture: remove the Leadership marker. PKK income -1 per Propaganda for the rest of the game [tune]. The PKK keeps its pieces. Capture does not end the game (CT lessons; F-021; F-045).

Evidence: Syria phases [F-020; E-0170; E-0078; E-0062]; KDP order of 1985, Oct 1992 attack, later alignment [E-0160; E-0082; F-022]; PUK as the more tolerant host [F-022]; host interests [F-051]. Iran stays event-only [F-025; E-0166].

rules.yaml.heading: Scope
rules.yaml.text: Legal Politics is a non-player system. It switches on in C3 with the HEP Founded card [E-0007; O-030]. In C1 and C2 Legal Space is Absent and this section does nothing. The rule set revises the Claude two-faction table (Claude scenarios file, section 3.4).

rules.yaml.heading: What Offices do
rules.yaml.text:
1. Offices sit in domestic spaces. They give no Control and are not PKK pieces (DD-10.2).
2. Agitation in their space may not go beyond Passive Opposition (DD-18.4).
3. They cap their space at Passive Support and at Passive Opposition (DD-18.4).
4. They add to neither victory score (DD-10.5).
5. They change Legitimacy: +1 at Propaganda if Legal Space is Open and 2 or more Offices are on the map; -1 extra for Village Clearance in an Office space; -2 for a ban.
6. The PKK cannot move Legal Space or Offices (DD-10.5). No PKK action reads or changes them. The game does not decide whether the parties acted independently of the PKK [F-018].

rules.yaml.heading: Closure filing
rules.yaml.text:
In the Legal Politics phase, before the procedure table, the State may file a closure case if Legal Space is Open or Prosecuted, at least one Office is on the map and no Closure Case marker is on the track. Place the Closure Case marker. Set Legal Space to Prosecuted. The case resolves at the next Propaganda round, line 1 below. Filing itself costs nothing (DD-10.4 puts the cost on the ban). An event that places the Closure Case marker also sets Legal Space to Prosecuted, as a filing does. Only the State executes such an event side (05, section 5.1).

The State's reason to file: Offices cap Diyarbakır City and Western Cities at Passive Support (and at Passive Opposition). The cost: Legitimacy -2 and Europe +1 at the ban, and loss of the Open-Space Legitimacy gain.

rules.yaml.heading: Procedure table
rules.yaml.text:
Run lines 1 to 6 in order in each Legal Politics phase from C3.

| Line | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Closure Case marker was on the track at the start of this phase | Ban: Legal Space to Banned. Place the Successor marker at the number of Offices on the map. Remove all Offices. Legitimacy -2. Europe +1. Remove the Closure Case marker. Stop. |
| 2 | Legal Space is Banned (line 1 did not apply) | Successor: Legal Space to Prosecuted. Place Offices equal to the Successor number minus 1 (minimum 1), using the line 4 order. Remove the Successor marker. Stop. |
| 3 | Legal Space is Open or Prosecuted | Office limit: Open 4, Prosecuted 3 [tune]. |
| 4 | Offices on the map are fewer than the limit | Place 1 Office in the first eligible space in this order: Diyarbakır City, Western Cities, Mardin, Van City, Şanlıurfa, Muş, Diyarbakır hinterland, Bingöl-Tunceli, Ağrı-Iğdır, Adıyaman, Elazığ. Eligible: Pop 2 or more, no Office, no PKK Control, not at Active Support or Active Opposition. |
| 5 | Offices on the map are more than the limit | Remove Offices from the eligible spaces latest in the line 4 order until at the limit. |
| 6 | Offices on the map equal the limit and no Closure Case marker is on the track | The prosecutor files: place the Closure Case marker. Line 1 bans at the next phase (DD-19.1). |

Notes:

1. Line 4 is a design convenience. It stops either armed player from choosing where legal politics exists (Sol non-player actors file).
2. Line 2 makes the successor return at the next round with fewer Offices (DD-10.3). History had successors ready before the ban: HADEP was founded 36 days before the DEP ban [E-0013; E-0014; F-015; F-052].
3. Events may place or remove Offices and move Legal Space as printed: HEP closure [E-0186; E-0009], DEP founding and closure [E-0010; E-0197; E-0014], HADEP founding and filing [E-0013; E-0236].
4. The 10 percent threshold kept the legal parties out of parliament [E-0153; F-016]. Offices stand for local presence, not seats.
5. Line 6 is the non-player prosecutor. Closure cases were brought by the Chief Public Prosecutor at the Court of Cassation [O-116], not by the cabinet. The State may still file earlier by choice (section 6.3). Line 6 keeps the founding, ban and successor cycle alive when the State player has no reason to file (IR-33; F-052).

rules.yaml.heading: Ceasefire (DD-11)
rules.yaml.text: The Ceasefire track has three steps: None, Declared and Reciprocal Restraint. A ceasefire is temporary and never ends the game. Designer decision of 2026-11-12 (`docs/audit/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, item 1): no settlement step exists, because Turkish territorial integrity and Kurdish independence are directly opposed.

rules.yaml.heading: Declaration
rules.yaml.text: From C3, the PKK may Declare Ceasefire as its action on a card, using the Limited Op box (05, section 2.3). Ceasefire must be None. Set it to Declared. Europe +1. Events may also declare for the PKK. Only the PKK declares (DD-11.2) [E-0089; E-0112; E-0123; E-0135; F-039].

rules.yaml.heading: Restrictions and breaches
rules.yaml.text:
| Ceasefire | PKK may not | State may not |
|---|---|---|
| Declared | Attack, Ambush, Strike Collaborators | No restriction. Each State Assault, Village Clearance, Cross-Border or Covert Action places the State Restraint Broken marker |
| Reciprocal Restraint | Attack, Ambush, Strike Collaborators, Coerce, place a domestic Base (DD-19.3) | Assault, Village Clearance, Cross-Border, Covert Action |

Breach: a faction that takes a forbidden action places its Restraint Broken marker and the Ceasefire goes to None. Free actions granted by events count as actions for this table. PKK breach: Europe -1. State breach (Reciprocal Restraint only): Legitimacy -2. A spoiler event may set the Ceasefire to None with no Restraint Broken marker and a neutral title; attribution stays as the sources state it [E-0091; E-0092; E-0093; F-038; F-053].

rules.yaml.heading: Ceasefire step (Propaganda, Legal Politics phase)
rules.yaml.text:
1. Declared, no State Restraint Broken marker: the State may accept. Ceasefire to Reciprocal Restraint. If it does not, the PKK keeps Declared or ends it (None). If the PKK ends a ceasefire that it declared by section 7.1, Europe -1, so a declaration that is not kept returns its Europe gain [tune].
2. Either faction may leave Reciprocal Restraint (to None) at this step. The State pays no cost. The PKK pays Europe -1 if it leaves Reciprocal Restraint for None (step 1 rule).

rules.yaml.heading: Not used
rules.yaml.text: This section held a settlement that ended the game. It is removed (Designer decision of 2026-11-12 (`docs/audit/OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, item 1)). Evidence: none of the historical ceasefires was recognized by the State [F-039]. The number is kept so that later section numbers do not change.

rules.yaml.heading: Steps
rules.yaml.text:
| Step | Drain at Propaganda | Unlocks | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Martial Law | -1 | none | Start Aug 1984 [E-0039; E-0052] |
| OHAL | -1 | Village Clearance (with OHAL Powers or C3+) | OHAL from 19 Jul 1987 [E-0055; F-013] |
| OHAL Extended Powers | -2 | Village Clearance; Sweep 1 per space | KHK 413 and 430 [E-0057; E-0058] |
| Normalizing | 0 | Return; no Village Clearance | Region shrank from 1994; Mardin out Nov 1996 [F-014; E-0219] |

rules.yaml.heading: Moves
rules.yaml.text:
1. Martial Law to OHAL: only by the OHAL card (mandatory in C2).
2. OHAL to OHAL Extended Powers: by the OHAL Powers card, or by a State step in Propaganda from C3.
3. In the Legitimacy phase (05, section 6.4, step 8) the State may move one step: OHAL to OHAL Extended Powers (from C3, step 2 above), OHAL Extended Powers to OHAL, OHAL to Normalizing or Normalizing to OHAL. Only Normalizing to OHAL costs Legitimacy (-1); the other steps are free. The track never returns to Martial Law (design choice).
4. Province-level changes are event effects only (DD-12.4) [E-0219]. Parliament renewed OHAL 46 times [Q-372; F-055].

rules.yaml.heading: Europe track
rules.yaml.text: Range 0 to 5 (04, section 3.6). Moves: PKK Rally on Europe +1; Declare Ceasefire +1; Serhildan +1; party ban +1; Propaganda harm comparison +1 or -1; State Diplomacy -1; Strike Collaborators -1; PKK breach -1; events. The Ban marker caps it at 3 [E-0194; E-0063; E-0064; Q-377; F-040]. US designation in 1997 is an event [E-0225; F-044]. Europe is not one patron. Voluntary support and coercion in diaspora funding stay distinct in card text [M-013].

rules.yaml.heading: Kurdish Hizbullah
rules.yaml.text:
Event-driven only. No player owns or orders it [M-016; F-058; F-057].

1. Card titles are neutral, for example "Unattributed killings in the southeast".
2. Effect: if any of Şırnak, Mardin, Diyarbakır City and Diyarbakır hinterland holds an Office, remove one Office from the highest-Pop such space. Otherwise remove one Guerrilla from the highest-Pop such space with a Guerrilla. Ties go in this order: Mardin, Diyarbakır City, Diyarbakır hinterland, Şırnak. The executing faction does not choose the target. Place a Disputed Harm marker there.
3. Attribution limit: a later event may turn a Disputed marker into a State Harm marker only if the card rests on a High or Moderate court or commission finding. Reported security-force links rest on a 1995 commission as relayed by HRW [F-058; E-0087]. No court has settled them.
4. Never print the "2,000 murders" figure [Q-403].

rules.yaml.heading: Covert violence
rules.yaml.text:
1. Covert Action is the only player tool for covert violence (06, section 3.5). Its markers are hidden, revealable and costly [M-009].
2. Reveal events: Susurluk [E-0015], commission reports [E-0109; E-0223], each revealing up to 2 Covert markers chosen at random.
3. Killings of legal-party and press figures with disputed perpetrators appear only as events with Disputed Harm markers and role names, never names [F-019; E-0098; E-0189; E-0193].
4. Court outcomes were mixed: convictions for the Susurluk gang and Agar, acquittals in JITEM cases [F-028; E-0242; E-0248; E-0249; E-0250]. Card text keeps that mix.

rules.yaml.heading: Tests
rules.yaml.text:
1. Count closure filings and successor returns per game. If the State never files, raise the Office cap effect.
2. Count the games that reach Reciprocal Restraint. If none does, lower the cost of State acceptance.
3. Check that the Legal Politics table never needs a judgment call. Two readers must place the same Offices.

rules.yaml.heading: What the deck contains
rules.yaml.text:
| Item | Count | Where |
|---|---:|---|
| Campaign pool cards (Events, Capabilities, Momentum) | 91 | Five pools, C1 to C5 |
| Deck-eligible pool cards | 91 | `deck_eligible = yes` |
| Research leads used as pool fillers | 0 | DK-013 and DK-014 were verified in R4 (section 3.3) |
| Pivotal Events | 4 | Two per faction, held in hand |
| Propaganda cards | 5 | One per pile |
| Structural (mandatory) cards | 7 | Inside the pools, marked in `design_note` |

A game uses 60 Event cards (5 piles of 12), 5 Propaganda cards and up to 4 Pivotal Events, as in the CT full scenario (CT 10.0). Pool cards that are not dealt stay out of the game unseen.

rules.yaml.heading: Deck structure and build procedure
rules.yaml.text: The build follows 05, section 1.1. This chapter adds the deck data and the rules for structural cards from DD-17.1.
subsections: 2.3 Capture must not be a dead card

rules.yaml.heading: Build each pile
rules.yaml.text:
Do this for C1, then C2, C3, C4 and C5:

1. Take the Campaign's structural cards. They are mandatory (DD-17.1).
2. Shuffle the other deck-eligible cards of that Campaign pool. Draw until the pile has 12 Event cards. Do not use research leads, except in a declared playtest (section 3.3).
3. Shuffle the 12 cards. Deal the top 8 face down.
4. If a structural card is in the bottom 4, swap it with the lowest non-structural card of the top 8. If a chain pair in section 8 ends in a structural card, the earlier card of that pair also counts as structural for this step.
5. Apply the order constraints in section 8 now, before the Propaganda card goes in.
6. Shuffle the Propaganda card into the bottom 4. Put the 8 on top. The Propaganda card is now card 9 to 13 of the pile.
7. Stack the piles with C1 on top.

Cards below a Propaganda card are played in the next Campaign (CT 10.0).

rules.yaml.heading: Structural cards
rules.yaml.text:
| Deck ID | Card | Campaign | Always line (applies on reveal) |
|---|---|---|---|
| DK-003 | Law 3175 | C1 | Move all 16 Village Guards from Out of Play to Available |
| DK-005 | KDP Orders PKK Out | C1 | If KDP is Host, set it to Tolerant |
| DK-019 | Syria Security Protocol | C2 | If Syria is Host, set it to Tolerant |
| DK-020 | OHAL | C2 | If Emergency Rule is Martial Law, set it to OHAL |
| DK-037 | HEP Founded | C3 | Legal Space to Open. Run Legal Politics lines 3 and 4 twice now |
| DK-040 | Northern Iraq Vacuum | C3 | From now on, Tolerant allows Cross-Border and PKK Bases in the KDP Zone and PUK Zone |
| DK-093 | Capture | C5 | If the Leadership is Abroad, apply Capture (07, section 5.2). If it is Present, do nothing |

Rules:

1. The Always lines copy 10, section 6.1 word for word in meaning.
2. The deck CSV has no Always column. The Always line is printed in the `design_note` field, after the words "structural, mandatory". On a printed card it goes above the two event texts.
3. Card type stays "Event" (DD-17.1). The Always line applies whether or not a faction executes the Event (05, section 5.7).
4. A Pivotal Event played on a structural card does not cancel its Always line (05, section 4, step 4).
5. C4 has no structural card (10, section 6.1).

rules.yaml.heading: Capture must not be a dead card
rules.yaml.text: The Capture Always line works only while the Leadership is Abroad. Two cards can flip it: the State Pivotal Coercive Diplomacy on Syria (DK-098) and the pool card PKK Leader Leaves Syria (DK-090). The Capture card also has an unshaded branch for a Present Leadership: Syria posture one step toward Hostile. So Capture always changes the board when the State takes it.

rules.yaml.heading: Faction order symbols
rules.yaml.text: Each card prints a two-symbol order, S-P or P-S, in the `faction_order` column. Chapter 05 gives this order no rule role. Eligibility comes from the Initiative track (DD-04). The symbols are kept for a future rule or for an optional module. Each pool has an equal or near-equal split (section 6). This is a gap, not a rule (section 10).

rules.yaml.heading: The rule
rules.yaml.text:
DD-13.3 says a card is deck-eligible when its event confidence is High or Moderate and at least one source with status "Verified source" stands behind the central fact. The rule as computed:

1. The central event is the first E- ID in the card's `event_ids`.
2. Event confidence is the `confidence` value of that event in `historical-events.csv`. It is not the card's own column.
3. The central fact test passes if at least one source ID is in both the card's `source_ids` and the central event's `source_ids`, and that source has `verification_status` "Verified source" in `source-registry.csv`.
4. Background rows are never eligible. They describe a period, not a discrete event: K-082, K-083, K-103, K-104, K-111 and K-112.
5. All other rows are "research lead".

The result is in the `deck_eligibility` column of the register. The `scenarios` column now holds the Campaign tag from the date (C1 to C5). Background rows get the tag of their period (K-111, dated "1990s", gets C3;C4;C5). Only K-112 (the 1982 Constitution) has no tag, because it predates the campaign. The old S1 to S5 tags are gone, because DD-01 replaced those scenarios.

rules.yaml.text:
| Campaign | Register rows | Deck-eligible in register | Pool in deck | Deck-eligible in pool | Pile size | Draw choice |

| C1 | 19 | 16 | 15 | 15 | 12 | 12 of 15 |

The register holds 159 rows. K-111 is counted in three Campaigns and K-112 in none. Eligible rows that are not in a pool stay in the register as reserves. Examples are the Akdivar judgment [K-090], the Saturday Mothers sit-in [K-060] and Article 8 amended [K-061]. The Pivotal source cards (K-006, K-052, K-053, K-072, K-074, K-114, K-115) leave the pools (section 4).

rules.yaml.heading: C1 meets the DD-13.2 minimum
rules.yaml.text:
C1 has 15 deck-eligible pool cards. DD-13.2 asks for 14. The C1 register has 16 eligible rows. One of them, K-006, is the source of the ARGK Formed Pivotal, so it cannot also be a pool card. The pool grew from 12 to 15 in the R4 verification:

1. DK-013 Border Attack and Air Raid into Northern Iraq [K-123; E-0165]. Raised from Low to Moderate. Two Turkish press retrospectives give the 15 Aug 1986 air raid [S-0532; S-0533] and a CSM report of 2 Sep 1986 gives the Turkish reprisal claim [S-0534]. The Uludere site comes only from Wikipedia. The card prints no casualty total (C-072).
2. DK-014 Human Rights Association Founded [K-124; E-0164]. Moderate. IHD's own page and a bianet history confirm the date and the 98 founders [S-0531; S-0530]. Both are IHD-derived, so the event stays Moderate. Soft effects only.
3. DK-100 Neighbors Condemn the Raid [K-158; E-0340]. New. Moderate. One contemporary report [S-0534].

The pile holds 12 cards, so each C1 game now draws 12 of 15. The leads no longer fill the pool. K-159 (martial law lifted in 11 more provinces, Mar 1985) is a research lead only: the source text could not be read [E-0341; S-0535].

rules.yaml.heading: Pivotal Events
rules.yaml.text:
The four Pivotals and their rules come from 05, section 4. Each faction holds both of its Pivotals from setup (10, section 2.3). The procedure is CT 2.3.7 as written in 05.

| Deck ID | Faction | Pivotal | Earliest | Board precondition | Effect | Evidence |

| DK-015 | PKK | ARGK Formed | C1 | 8 or more Guerrillas in domestic spaces and at least 2 domestic PKK Bases | Place up to 4 Guerrillas in spaces with PKK Bases. Flip all Guerrillas there Underground. PKK +3 Resources | [E-0075] |

rules.yaml.heading: Rules for card text
rules.yaml.text:
1. Name the act plainly: killed, burned, displaced. No euphemism and no glory words. Titles use places and roles, not victims' names.
2. No card gives points or Resources for killing. No card removes a piece and then pays for the removal.
3. A T2 card where one faction caused the harm has a block-only side for that faction. The harmer may take the Event to choose where the Harm marker goes, but gains nothing else. Examples: DK-030 İkikaya and DK-059 Bingöl Road Killings for the PKK; DK-033 custody abuse and DK-043 Newroz for the State.
4. The Harm marker names the faction that caused the harm. Where attribution is contested, the marker is Disputed (05, section 5.8; DD-15.4).
5. Cards print no death or displacement totals. The Playbook gives a range with its source [C-006; C-024; C-029].
6. Unattributed killings follow 07, section 10.1. The executing faction does not choose the target (DK-053).
7. Covert reveals follow 07, section 10.2. Up to 2 markers, at random (DK-079, DK-080).
8. Low-confidence events carry no hard effect (DD-15.4). No Low card is in a pool. DK-013 rose to Moderate in R4.
9. A T2 or T3 card needs a content note in the Playbook before any public playtest.

rules.yaml.heading: Tests
rules.yaml.text:
1. Deal 20 piles per Campaign. Count how often each chain pair needs a swap. More than 1 swap per pile on average means the chain list is too long.
2. Track Event choices per faction per Campaign. If either faction takes the Event on fewer than 1 card in 4, its sides are too weak.
3. Track Legitimacy across the five Campaigns with only Events and no Village Clearance. If it reaches 0 before C4, reduce the State cost cards in C3 and C4.
4. Check that no block-only side is ever the best choice for the harmer except to block the other side. If it is, the harm cost is too low.
5. DK-090 at Syria Restricted gives the same result as the State Pivotal Coercive Diplomacy on Syria without its Legitimacy precondition. Count how often the State uses DK-090 to skip the Pivotal. If often, add the Legitimacy 5 test to DK-090.

rules.yaml.heading: Victory scores
rules.yaml.text:
| Faction | Score | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| State | Total Support + Legitimacy | DD-14.2. Total Support = Pop at Passive Support + 2 x Pop at Active Support |
| PKK | Total Opposition + PKK Bases in domestic spaces | DD-14.3. Total Opposition = Pop at Passive Opposition + 2 x Pop at Active Opposition |

Rules:

1. Count only the 13 domestic spaces. External boxes and their Bases never count (DD-14.4).
2. Displaced spaces keep their Pop (DD-07.3). A displaced space keeps the level that Village Clearance left (one level toward Neutral, DD-18.3) and scores at that level.
3. No term counts kills, casualties, removed pieces or displacement (DD-07.4; M-028).
4. Control is not in either score. A controlled space can stay politically unsettled (CT 1.6 to 1.7; F-049).

Basis: CT 1.9 and 7.2 (Support + Commitment against Opposition + Bases), with Legitimacy in place of Commitment. CT lessons reject Commitment as "political will"; Legitimacy here records acceptance of State conduct, not willingness to fight (DD-03.3).

rules.yaml.heading: Method
rules.yaml.text:
1. **Easy ceiling.** Take the start board. Move every space that starts at Support (State) or Opposition (PKK) to the Active level. Add start Legitimacy (State) or start domestic Bases (PKK). This is the score a faction can reach without winning any contested space.
2. **Threshold** = easy ceiling + (rough maximum - easy ceiling) / 3, round down [tune].

Reason: the first draft measured the gap from the start score. The desk test in 11 showed that the State then reached 42 in the first Campaign only by moving its four safe Passive Support spaces to Active (IR-01, IR-02 in `../audit/independent-critical-review.md`). Measuring from the easy ceiling makes each faction win about one third of the contested headroom. Confidence: Moderate; this is one paper run.

rules.yaml.heading: Campaign (Aug 1984 setup in 10, section 2)
rules.yaml.text:
Rough maximums:

1. Total Support or Total Opposition: every domestic space at the Active level = 2 x 33 = 66 (Pop 33, DD-22).
2. State: 66 + Legitimacy 20 = 86.
3. PKK: 66 + 12 domestic Bases (all 12 PKK Bases; Western Cities excluded) = 78.

Start scores:

1. State: Passive Support in Western Cities (3), Şanlıurfa (4), Elazığ (2) and Adıyaman (2) = Total Support 11. Legitimacy 10. Score 21.
2. PKK: Passive Opposition in Şırnak (1), Siirt (1), Hakkari (1), Batman hinterland (1) and Van hinterland (1) = Total Opposition 5. Domestic Bases 1 (Şırnak). Score 6.

| Faction | Start | Easy ceiling | Maximum | Headroom | Headroom / 3 | Method value | Threshold [tune] |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| State | 21 | 2 x 11 + 10 = 32 | 86 | 54 | 18 | 50 | 49 |
| PKK | 6 | 2 x 5 + 1 = 11 | 78 | 67 | 22 | 33 | 32 |

The thresholds in use are designer decisions, not the method values:

1. State 49: kept when DD-22 raised Pop from 32 to 33 (DD-22 item 11).
2. PKK 32 (designer decision, 17 Nov 2026; `docs/prototype/35-start-setup-options-draft.md`). The method value 33 counts Batman hinterland and Van hinterland as easy ground. Van hinterland, Hakkari and Siirt are not under PKK Control and hold no PKK Base, so the PKK cannot Agitate there at the start (rules 3.6.2). Counting only the spaces where it can (Şırnak, Batman hinterland) gives 31. 32 lies between the two. Confidence: Low. Re-run the qualification set before relying on it.

Example boards that reach a threshold (illustration, not prediction):

1. State 49: Legitimacy 12 and Total Support 37, for example Active Support in Western Cities (6), Şanlıurfa (8), Elazığ (4) and Adıyaman (4), plus Passive Support in Mardin, Batman hinterland and Batman City (4), Diyarbakır City (2), Diyarbakır hinterland (2), Van City, Van hinterland and Bitlis (4) and Ağrı-Iğdır (3).
2. PKK 32: Active Opposition in Şırnak and Siirt (4), Hakkari (2) and Diyarbakır City (4), Passive Opposition in Mardin, Batman hinterland and Batman City (4), Muş and Bingöl-Tunceli (4) and Van City, Van hinterland and Bitlis (4) = 22, plus 10 domestic Bases.

rules.yaml.heading: Victory check (each Propaganda round except the first)
rules.yaml.text:
At the Victory phase (05, section 6.1), skipped in the first Propaganda round of every scenario (CT 6.1):

1. Compute both scores and both Harm counts. Count each face-down Covert marker as revealed for this check: State score -2 and State Harm count +1 per marker. Do not flip the markers. Reason: Scenario B has its only check before the final reveal, so hidden markers escaped their cost at a winning check (11, section 6; IR-34).
2. A faction qualifies if its score reaches or exceeds its threshold and its Harm count is at or below its Harm limit.
3. If exactly one faction qualifies, it wins. The game ends.
4. If both qualify, the higher margin wins (CT 7.1). Margin = score - threshold.
5. If neither qualifies, play on.

rules.yaml.heading: Harm gate
rules.yaml.text:
Harm limit: 6 for each faction [tune].

1. State Harm count = State Harm markers on the map.
2. PKK Harm count = PKK Harm markers + Coercion markers on the map (04, section 4.2).
3. Disputed markers count for neither.
4. Face-down Covert markers count at a victory check as step 1 says. All are revealed before final scoring (05, section 6.6).

A faction above its limit cannot win at a check (DD-14.2, DD-14.3). It can still lower its count by Redress (07, section 1.3).

rules.yaml.heading: Final scoring
rules.yaml.text:
After phase 6.6 of the final Propaganda round:

1. Reveal all Covert markers. Each becomes a State Harm marker and costs Legitimacy 2.
2. Recompute scores and Harm counts.
3. Final margin = score - threshold - 2 x (Harm count - Harm limit, if above 0) [tune].
4. The higher final margin wins (CT 7.3). Negative margins still rank.
5. Ties: the faction with the lower Harm count wins. If still tied, the PKK wins (CT 7.1, ties to the insurgent).

Result labels for the record sheet: a difference of 5 or less is a "narrow" result; 6 or more is a "clear" result (CT 8.6 pattern).

rules.yaml.heading: Perverse incentive check
rules.yaml.text: Test: does any harmful action raise its user's margin relative to the opponent? Relative change = change in own margin - change in opponent's margin.

rules.yaml.heading: Emptying spaces (Village Clearance)
rules.yaml.text:
Target Pop P. Village Clearance shifts the space one level toward Neutral (DD-18.3). From Passive Opposition the PKK loses P; from Active Opposition it loses P (the space falls to Passive). The State loses 2P Legitimacy at once and 1 more at the next Propaganda round (06, section 3.4).

| Case | State margin change | PKK margin change | Relative change for the State |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P = 4, Active Opposition | -8 now, -9 by next round | -4 | -4 now, -5 by next round |
| P = 4, Passive Opposition | -8 now, -9 | -4 | -4, then -5 |
| P = 1, Active Opposition | -2 now, -3 | -1 | -1, then -2 |
| P = 3, Neutral | -6 now, -7 | 0 | -6, then -7 |

The relative change is never positive. The State Harm marker adds to the Harm gate and, beyond the limit, costs 2 margin at the end. The Reception marker can add a further -1 Legitimacy. Pop never falls, so thresholds never fall (DD-07.3). The legality floor (Legitimacy at least 2P + 1) stops the State from clearing at zero cost when Legitimacy is near 0. Result: emptying a space never pays in relative score. Its gain is military: activation and a Rally block. Limit of this test: a victory check is a threshold test, not a relative test. When the PKK is within P of its threshold, Village Clearance can still deny a PKK win at the next check although the State loses more points. DD-18.3 halved this effect against Active Opposition. It stays a watch item (11, section 3).

rules.yaml.heading: Rewarding killing
rules.yaml.text:
| Action | Score effect for the user | Cost | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assault removing Guerrillas | 0 | Resources | No reward for removal |
| Assault removing a domestic PKK Base | PKK -1 | Resources | Infrastructure loss, not a kill count. No State gain |
| PKK Attack | 0 | Resources, attrition | No reward for removal |
| Strike Collaborators | 0 | 1 Resource, PKK Harm marker, Europe -1 | Net negative |
| Covert Action | 0 now; -2 Legitimacy on reveal, and -2 per face-down marker at every victory check (section 3, step 1) | Harm marker | Net negative |
| Cross-Border Assault | 0 (external Bases never count) | Resources, Disputed marker | No score reward |

No action adds points for removing pieces or for harm. Indirect effect: Strike Collaborators, Covert Action, Attack and Assault can change Control, and Control opens or closes Civic Action and Agitation in a space. The PKK Harm marker from Strike Collaborators blocks shifts toward Opposition in its own space, which closes that route there. Playtest must log any Control flip from a harm action that leads to a score shift in the same Campaign.

rules.yaml.heading: Coercion (watch item)
rules.yaml.text: Coerce on a Pop P space at Support lowers the State score by P. The PKK pays 1 Resource and takes a Coercion marker, which counts toward its Harm gate until Reset removes it. This is the CT Terror pattern (CT 3.3.4) and DD-06.5 allows it. It is intimidation, not killing. Bound: 8 Coercion markers exist; with the limit at 6, a PKK that holds 7 or more Harm points cannot win at a check and loses 2 margin per point at the end. Playtest must log Coerce use. If Coerce is the cheapest PKK path to victory in more than one game in three, raise its cost or make the marker last two Resets.

rules.yaml.heading: Other checks
rules.yaml.text:
1. Banning the legal party lifts the Passive Support and Passive Opposition caps in Office spaces (DD-18.4); it opens the same room for PKK Agitation. State gain is at most 2 (Diyarbakır City) + 3 (Western Cities) Total Support and needs Civic Action spending. Cost: Legitimacy -2, Europe +1, loss of the Open-Space gain. This is a political trade-off, not a harm reward. Log it.
2. Stalling: ties go to the PKK, so the State cannot win by passing.
3. Displacement into cities never moves Pop, so the State cannot raise Pop in spaces it controls (Claude harm file, section 5).

6. Civic Action, rules as drafted (Control and Police): cap 10. Van-Bitlis 2 shifts (4), Şanlıurfa 1 (2), Mardin-Batman 1 (2), Diyarbakır City 1 (2). Total Support 15 to 33. **State score 43, above its threshold of 42 in the first round.**
7. Agitation: no space has a PKK piece and no State Control except Bingöl-Muş, which is already at Active Opposition. The PKK spends 0. PKK score 13.
8. Redeploy and Reset: Troops return to Bases and Cities, Guerrillas flip Underground, Campaign C2, PKK First.

Rerun of step 6 with the fix now in 07, section 1.3 (Propaganda Civic Action also needs Troops, as CT 6.3.1 does). With the same card play, only Mardin-Batman and Van-Bitlis qualify: State 37, margin -5. But that card play moved Troops out of both Cities before the rule existed. A State that knows the rule takes Air Mobility Troops from Elazığ, Dersim and Ağrı instead and keeps Troops in both Cities. Then Van-Bitlis 2 shifts (4), Mardin-Batman 1 (2), Western Cities 1 (2) and Diyarbakır City 1 (2) give Total Support 32 and **State score 42 in round 1 again**. PKK 13, margin -15.

Coordinator recheck under DD-18 (easy-ceiling threshold 49, Propaganda Civic Action cap Legitimacy / 2). Same planned play: base Total Support 15, cap 10 / 2 = 5 Resources, so at most 2 shifts (Van-Bitlis twice, +8). Total Support 23, **State score 33, margin -16** in round 1. Round 2 estimate: C2 cards DK-024, DK-026 and DK-032 can raise Legitimacy to 16, so the cap rises to 8 (4 shifts, up to about +14), plus Train Civic Action during C2. If the PKK never Coerces or Agitates in Support spaces, the State can reach about 50 at the round 2 check (1989). With PKK contest it should fall short. Round 5: 49 is clearly reachable, so the two brakes do not overshoot. Verdict: round 1 fixed; a round 2 State win stays possible against a passive PKK. This is paper arithmetic, not play. Confidence: low to medium.

rules.yaml.heading: Desk-test verdict
rules.yaml.text:
The rules can be played card by card without a referee, after five clarifications. The draft as written produced a degenerate result: a State threshold score in the first Propaganda round from sensible play. The Troops requirement (kept for CT 6.3.1 fidelity) does not remove it: a State that plans for the rule still scores 42 in round 1. With Resources left and three State-friendly C2 cards (DK-024, DK-026 and DK-032 each give Legitimacy +2), the State will very likely pass 42 at the round 2 check unless the PKK Coerces Support spaces. That fails the 10, section 8, test 2 criterion on paper. Confidence: medium. One run, one player.

ARGK variant: after DK-001 the PKK had 8 domestic Guerrillas and the Botan Base. Under the first fix ("in domestic spaces") ARGK was still legal on card 2. It beat the logged play: +3 Resources, +4 Guerrillas, the State loses the DK-012 Event and the PKK keeps First Eligible. The precondition now also needs 2 domestic PKK Bases. In this log that point comes on card 8.

rules.yaml.heading: Ambiguities and degenerate points found
rules.yaml.text:
1. ARGK Formed needed "8 or more Guerrillas on the map". The setup counts external boxes as on the map (10, section 2.2 totals), so the Pivotal was legal on card 1 in Aug 1984 for an event of Oct 1986 [E-0075]. With "in domestic spaces" alone it was still legal and dominant on card 2. Fixed: 8 Guerrillas in domestic spaces and 2 domestic PKK Bases. Timing stays a watch item.
2. Air Mobility "among up to 3 domestic spaces" did not say whether origins count. Fixed to the CT 4.2.2 reading.
3. Western Cities lockout. The PKK cannot March there, may Rally in a City only at Neutral or Opposition, and Western Cities starts at Passive Support. No card shifts it or places PKK pieces there (deck search). So 3 to 6 State points were safe for the whole game. Fixed: Rally in Western Cities is legal at Passive Support [tune].
4. Responder matrix. The Event row was labeled "design choice". The CT playbook twelfth-card example shows Op + SA or Pass after a Pivotal in the Event box. Relabeled. Note 1 described a British Way option (select the Event box, then pass) that this track cannot do. Rewritten.
5. Martial Law and OHAL drain -1, and the restraint gain gives +1 whenever no Displacement marker flips. In C1 and C2 the Emergency Rule costs nothing. Open (proposal in section 3).
6. State Resources run dry by card 4, then the State earns 19 against 6 per round. Ops cost the State 2 per space and the PKK 1. Open watch item.
7. Train option 3 turns 2 Police into a State Base for 2 Resources. In Şanlıurfa this adds Pop 4 to State income at every round. Open watch item.
8. Attack with 6 or more Guerrillas never fails (die result less than or equal to 6). CT has the same rule. Logged only.
9. Campaign length. With the Propaganda card at position 9 to 13, a Campaign has 8 to 16 cards (12 + this pile's position - last pile's position). DD-13.1 says about 9 to 12. Proposed DD text change.

rules.yaml.heading: Full-campaign arithmetic
rules.yaml.text:
1. Piece counts in setups A, B and C match the inventory and the printed totals. Control and scores in all three tables recompute correctly.
2. Pop values recompute from 1990 totals with half-up rounding and a minimum of 1: sum 29 plus 3 for Western Cities.
3. Thresholds recomputed by the one-third rule at review time (42 / 28, 41 / 34 and 38 / 40). After this review the coordinator adopted the easy-ceiling rule and a Civic Action cap of Legitimacy / 2 (DD-18): 49 / 30, 48 / 41 and 44 / 48.
4. Resources over five Campaigns, no events: State about 19 a round at start, more with each new Base in a Plain or Mountain space. PKK about 6 at start, then lower: the KDP order and the Syria protocol cut host income, and Capture removes 1 more. Estimate: State 95 to 130, PKK 20 to 30 plus Extort. The cost gap is 2 to 1, the income gap is 3 or 4 to 1. Low confidence; design currency only.
5. Legitimacy under OHAL Extended Powers: -2 drain, +1 restraint, net -1 per round before any Clearance. A State that never clears loses at most 3 points over C3 to C5 from the drain.

rules.yaml.heading: Historian of Turkey
rules.yaml.text:
1. Start conditions are defensible: martial law in force since Dec 1978 and Law 2935 from 1983 [E-0039; E-0052]. The OHAL card date is right [E-0055].
2. Batman and Şırnak names are handled as regions, with a scenario note (03, section 7). Good practice.
3. The fixed C2 cards give three Legitimacy +2 gains (local elections, the lawyer access decree, refugees admitted). Each is sourced. Together they make 1987 to 1989 a good period for State Legitimacy. That reading is arguable for a period with documented custody abuse [E-0295]. Watch in play.

rules.yaml.heading: Kurdish studies
rules.yaml.text:
1. Support and Opposition are labeled as abstractions of active minorities (DD-06.2). Good.
2. Offices block all PKK Agitation in their space but only cap State Support at Passive. The legal party thus harms the PKK more than the State. This is a quiet claim about C-025 (party autonomy) through a mechanic. Proposed DD-10.5 change: an Office caps its space at Passive Support and at Passive Opposition, and blocks Agitation only beyond Passive Opposition.
3. Guards are State pieces with no own aim [F-057]. The deck adds guard refusal without violence (DK-031). Good.

rules.yaml.heading: Security studies
rules.yaml.text:
1. Detection before destruction, the Mountain modifier and Guards that help detection but not Assault fit the evidence base [F-049; F-059].
2. Cross-Border places a Disputed marker that records "unknown". That is honest.
3. Village Clearance gives activation and a Rally block. Its threshold denial value is not costed (section 3).

rules.yaml.heading: Quantitative
rules.yaml.text:
1. All arithmetic in setups, thresholds and Pop checks out (section 1.7).
2. The threshold method assumes both sides grow at a similar rate. The desk test shows the State grows much faster, because its Support sits in safe Plain spaces and Western Cities. The one-third rule gives equal gaps, not equal difficulty.
3. Five-level Support doubles the headroom of every space against CT. Test 2 in 04, section 6 (count Active once) should run early.

rules.yaml.heading: COIN designer
rules.yaml.text:
1. The CT initiative track is applied correctly. Pass, Limited Op and Event keep the First Eligible faction First (CT 2.3.5).
2. Civic Action was looser than CT 6.3.1. Fixed for the Propaganda phase, but the fix does not change the pace problem.
3. The Base income term rewards Train option 3 too well. Try "Pop of spaces with State Control, a State Base and Troops".
4. Stale cross-references in 03, 05, 08 and the deck notes were fixed.

rules.yaml.heading: Playtester
rules.yaml.text:
1. The Legitimacy phase has eight steps. In C1 and C2 most of them do nothing. A C1 and C2 play aid can skip steps 2 to 5.
2. The State is idle for two cards per Campaign for lack of Resources. That gives the PKK free tempo. It may be fine. Log Pass counts (05, section 10, test 3).
3. The PKK path to score is clear: March into a lightly held space, Rally a Base, Agitate in the Rally. The State path is clear: Train with Civic Action in Pop 4 spaces. Both are understandable in one game.

rules.yaml.heading: Ethics
rules.yaml.text:
1. No action adds score for removing pieces or for harm. The relative test in 09, section 7.1 holds.
2. Village Clearance can still decide a game by denial at a threshold check. That is a reward for emptying a space in outcome terms, if not in points. Proposed DD-07.2 change in section 3.
3. Harm actions can flip Control and so open or close Civic Action and Agitation. 09, section 7.2 now names this. The PKK Harm marker self-block covers Strike Collaborators in its own space only.
4. Block-only sides for the harmer on T2 cards are a good rule. DK-018 (contested Pınarcık killings) gives its PKK side a Redress anywhere for 2 Resources. That is the normal Agitation price, so no discount. Logged.

rules.yaml.heading: Traceability
rules.yaml.text:
1. Thirty factual sentences across 20 Package A files were checked against their rows: 24 match, 3 minor mismatches, 3 overstated. Four one-line corrections were applied. Details are in the audit file.
2. E-0082 has confidence Moderate in its field but its notes say Low until a primary source is seen. Proposed data fix.
3. Every cited ID in the chapters exists (validator: 0 unknown IDs).

rules.yaml.heading: Design risks
rules.yaml.text: This section merges the useful parts of the Claude self-critique and counterfactual file and the Sol counterfactual and critical review files. MOD-3B and Cohesion items stay in the optional modules chapter and are not repeated.

rules.yaml.heading: Risks that the desk test confirmed
rules.yaml.text:
| Risk | Evidence in this review | Mitigation now | Next step |
|---|---|---|---|
| State Support runaway | 43 in round 1 as drafted; still 42 with the Troops rule if the State plans for it | Troops needed for Propaganda Civic Action (CT fidelity only) | Retune thresholds or cap Civic Action at Legitimacy / 2; run two-sided tests |
| Income asymmetry | 19 v 6 per round at start | none | Log per-Campaign income; try the Troops test on the Base term |
| Threshold denial by Village Clearance | Relative test holds, threshold test does not | 09, section 7.1 now names it | Proposed DD-07.2: Clearance shifts one level toward Neutral, not to Neutral |
| Emergency Rule costs nothing in C1 and C2 | Drain -1 always offset by +1 | none | Restraint gain only if the State placed no Harm marker in the Campaign |
| Office asymmetry | Office blocks all Agitation, caps Support at Passive | none | Proposed DD-10.5 change (section 2.2) |

rules.yaml.heading: Risks from the input reviews that still apply
rules.yaml.text:
1. **Weak evidence base for effects.** Every card effect and every number is a hypothesis (DD-15.1). Card events are sourced; card sizes are not. Risk high for values, moderate for facts.
2. **Historical determinism.** Seven mandatory structural cards fix the large changes in order. This is honest for law and institutions (Law 3175, OHAL, HEP). It is less safe for hosts. The Syria protocol card always moves Syria to Tolerant, but its shaded side can move it back. Capture fires only if the Leadership is Abroad, so it is conditional, as the data call the sanctuary-capture link an inference [F-021]. Do not tune thresholds so that the historical path wins.
3. **The opposite error.** A design where the PKK wins easily would imply that a small change was enough. The data do not show that. The desk test shows the reverse risk now: the State wins too easily.
4. **False balance.** The inventory is about 2 to 1, and real ratios were larger (04, section 1). Both armed sides carry harm costs, and the Harm limit is 6 for each. DD-15.3 says equal costs do not claim equal acts. Card text must name each act with its evidence level.
5. **False precision.** Tracks and thresholds suggest measurement. No source number becomes a threshold (M-028). Keep the "[design]" label on every Pop value.
6. **Normalizing violence.** Village Clearance, Covert Action and Strike Collaborators carry plain print names and costs. Players may still treat them as tools. A content note and an opt-out rule for T2 cards are needed before any public playtest (08, section 7.2).
7. **Exoticism.** Kurds are not one block: the PKK, Guards, the legal parties, Hizbullah and tribes had opposed interests [F-057]. The two-player core keeps legal politics as a non-player system. That loses a human advocate for legal actors (Sol review). MOD-3B is the tested remedy.
8. **Source bias.** Most data are in English. Turkish and Kurdish-language sources are under-represented. Several C1 cards rest on one source family (08, section 10).
9. **Consultation.** No Kurdish or Turkish scholars, civil-society members or survivors have reviewed the design. This must happen before any public release.

rules.yaml.heading: Counterfactual play paths the rules allow
rules.yaml.text:
The deck fixes the frame. Players change the board, not the facts on a card. A counterfactual result is a game result, not evidence about the past. Plausible for game purposes means: the actor existed, held the instrument and faced the choice. It does not mean likely.

| Path | Rules that allow it | What the data show | What the data do not show |
|---|---|---|---|
| State never uses Village Clearance | Clearance is an optional SA; restraint gain +1 per round | Clearance cut PKK logistics early and cost later [F-050] | What a different field policy would have done |
| Earlier Normalizing | After the OHAL card the State may step to Normalizing; drain 0, Return legal | The emergency region shrank from 1994 [F-014] | Whether earlier normalization would have reduced violence |
| Ceasefire holds | Declare Ceasefire from C3; Reciprocal Restraint (07, section 7) | The 1993 ceasefire was declared and collapsed [E-0089; F-038]; the State recognized none [F-039] | Whether any ceasefire could have held; responsibility for the collapse is disputed |
| Legal party never banned | Closure filing is a State choice (07, section 6.3) | Each closure was followed by a successor [F-052] | Whether the legal channel would have reduced the war |
| PKK avoids coercion | Coerce and Strike Collaborators are optional | Both armed sides pressed the same villages [F-034] | The political payoff of restraint |
| Syria pressure earlier or later | Diplomacy SA from C1 (with -1 before C5); Pivotal from C5 | Syria yielded in 1998 under threats [F-020] | Whether earlier pressure would have worked |
| KDP and PUK kept apart | Separate posture tracks; no automatic link (DD-09.1) | The hosts acted on their own interests [F-051] | Exact timing of any alternative alignment |
| Leadership never Abroad | Capture needs Abroad; Present makes the Always line do nothing | Capture followed the departure from Syria [F-021] | That capture was inevitable or impossible |

Excluded by scope: a Turkish invasion of Syria, a pan-Kurdish state and an all-Kurdish coalition player. These are scope choices, not claims about what actors imagined.

Debrief questions after each game:

1. Which card most changed your plan?
2. Which action cost you later, and did the delay surprise you?
3. What could the actors do that the game did not let you do?
4. What did the game let you do that the actors could not?
5. Which result do you think the game got wrong?

Testing rule: record every win that used an unhistorical path. A high win rate for one path means the rules reward a path the history does not support or fail to model its cost. Treat both as design bugs, never as a finding about history.

rules.yaml.heading: Residual risks
rules.yaml.text:
1. **Critical: State threshold pace.** Even with the Troops rule, the State reaches its threshold in round 1 on paper, so a State win at the first victory check (round 2) is likely. Thresholds are [tune] under DD-14.6. Two options to test first: (a) Propaganda Civic Action cap = Legitimacy / 2, round down; (b) State threshold computed from a "contested maximum" that leaves out Western Cities. Run 10, section 8, test 2 before any other tuning.
2. **Major: income asymmetry and the Base term.** Log income per Campaign. If the State ends any Campaign with more than 20 unspent Resources in more than one game in three, cut the base income from 8 to 6.
3. **Major: threshold denial by Village Clearance.** Proposed DD-07.2 change. Until then, log every Clearance made when the PKK is within 2 x Pop of its threshold.
4. **Moderate: Office asymmetry** (proposed DD-10.5 change).
5. **Moderate: Emergency Rule has no cost in C1 and C2.** Test the restraint-gain change.
6. **Moderate: C1 has little draw variety** (12 of 15 cards). DK-013 and DK-014 were verified in R4 and DK-100 was added, which closed the DD-13.2 shortfall.
7. **Moderate: Western Cities fix is untested.** The new Rally right may make Western Cities a cheap PKK target. Count Rally and Coerce there (03, section 8, test 3).
8. **Minor: CT ambiguity on responder locations** (05, section 2.3, note 2) is now labeled a design choice.
9. **Not tested here:** C3 to C5 systems (Legal Politics, ceasefire, Covert Action, Capture). The next desk test should start Scenario B and play one full Legal Politics phase and one ceasefire step.

Next step: run Scenario A twice with sides swapped and the fixes in place. Log the round 2 margins (10, section 8, test 1).

rules.yaml.heading: Findings
rules.yaml.text:
Major:

1. IR-31: the PKK could execute State-owned legal-politics sides and so file a case or force a ban that costs the State. Fixed in 05, section 5.1.
2. IR-33: after that fix, only the State holds a Legal Politics decision, and it has no reason to file. Proposed DD-10.4 change.
3. IR-34: face-down Covert markers escaped their cost at a victory check. Fixed in 09, section 3.
4. IR-35: Legitimacy 0 made bans and State breaches free. Fixed in 04, section 3.2.
5. IR-36: the Western Cities lockout came back at Active Support. Fixed in 03 and 06.
6. IR-37: the State threshold of 48 was out of reach. Open.
7. IR-38: Coerce was the most efficient action in the run. Open.

Moderate: IR-32 (Office in an Active space; fixed), IR-39 (Europe saturates; open), IR-40 (Serhildan legal on card 1; open), IR-41 (restraint asymmetry; open), IR-42 (free Declare Ceasefire; fixed), IR-43 (Cross-Border Sweep has no lasting effect; open), IR-44 (Emergency Rule step list; fixed), IR-45 (external Base rule; fixed), IR-46 (Village Clearance is dominated; logged).

Minor: IR-47, IR-48, IR-49, IR-50, IR-51 and IR-52 (fixed), IR-53 (logged).

rules.yaml.heading: Verdict
rules.yaml.text:
1. Playability: the C3 and C4 rules can be played card by card. Fourteen text defects needed a ruling or a fix. Most sat in 07 (Legal Politics, ceasefire, Emergency Rule).
2. Balance (paper only): Scenario B tilts hard to the PKK. The State peaked at 26 on card 2 and fell to 10 by the end of the C3 round. Drivers: Coerce (card 8), Legitimacy drains with Europe fixed at 5 and a Propaganda Civic Action cap of 0 at Legitimacy 0 or 1. About 6 points of the Legitimacy loss came from harm tools used to exercise them (Clearance and the Covert reveal). A State that skips both and is not hit by a PKK filing ends C3 near Legitimacy 8 and a score of about 18 to 24 (estimate), still far from 48. The PKK at 26 needs 15 more and lost 5 net over the first 5 C4 cards against heavy State spending. Expect margins to decide the game, with a clear PKK result. Confidence: low (one run, one player).
3. Ethics: no direct score for harm. Three indirect payoffs: a ban forced by the PKK (fixed), free State harm at Legitimacy 0 (fixed) and Extort income after a Strike Collaborators Control flip (logged, IR-13 pattern). Village Clearance never paid.
4. Legal Politics (DD-02 test): not passive on cards, because both armed players raced to set levels before Offices arrived. In the Propaganda phase only the State has a lever and no reason to use it. This is one data point toward the DD-02 flip trigger, not a trigger.

Next step: rerun Scenario B with the fixes and sides swapped, to the C4 Propaganda round. Log the round 2 check and the successor line (10, section 8, test 1).

rules.yaml.heading: Purpose
rules.yaml.text:
1. Find missing procedures and dominant strategies before more content work.
2. Check that harmful actions never pay in score (M-028; 09, section 7).
3. Decide between the CT initiative track and the Sol alternative on recorded evidence (DD-04).
4. Decide whether the MOD-3B module becomes the default for C3 to C5 (DD-02 flip trigger).

The plan does not measure balance. Ten games can show severe exploits, not equal win chances between asymmetric sides (Sol 16; 13, section A.9). All counts are pass or fail screens.

rules.yaml.heading: Order of scenarios and a change to the build order
rules.yaml.text:
Test order:

1. **Stage 0: desk test of Scenario A (1984-1989, C1 and C2).**
2. **Stage 1: desk tests of Scenario B (1990-1995) and Scenario C (1993-1999).**
3. **Stage 2: two-player sessions of A, B and C.**
4. **Stage 3: the full campaign (C1 to C5).**
5. **Stage 4: optional modules (MOD-3B, then MOD-4A, then Concept B).**
6. **Stage 5: outside readers.**

Reason for Scenario A first:

1. It has the fewest systems. Legal Politics, Covert Action, Declare Ceasefire, Serhildan and both State Pivotals are off (10, section 6.2). Errors in the core engine show without noise from late systems.
2. A broken C1 breaks every campaign.
3. It tests the structural switch rules early: Law 3175 and OHAL are mandatory cards in C1 and C2 (M-032).

This differs from 02, section 6, step 1 (C4 slice first). C4 holds the most structural change and is the worst place to find core errors. Chapter 02, section 6 needs a matching change, recorded in the decisions file, before this order is binding.

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 0: desk test of Scenario A
rules.yaml.text:
1. One facilitator plays both sides with open information. This is a rules walkthrough, not a blind test. Do not report it as one (Sol 16).
2. Use the full campaign setup (10, section 2) and piles C1 and C2 (05, section 1.1).
3. After each action, write down the best alternative and why it was worse (Sol 16).
4. Fix each missing procedure through a written design decision, never by a ruling at the table (Sol 16).
5. Play at least 3 deck seeds in each initiative arm (6 games). Plot Legitimacy by round for all games before any tuning (Claude 03, Stage 0).
6. Run the CT initiative comparison (section 6) in this stage, before any other value change.
7. Exit: two clean games with no new missing procedure and the checks in section 5.1 all passed.

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 1: desk tests of Scenarios B and C
rules.yaml.text:
1. Same method as Stage 0. Scenario B adds Legal Politics, Village Clearance, Covert Action, Declare Ceasefire, Serhildan and (in C4) Area Domination. Scenario C adds Coercive Diplomacy on Syria, Return and Capture (10, sections 4 and 5).
2. Play adversarial strategies (section 7) against each new system.
3. Exit: two clean games per scenario.

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 2: two-player sessions
rules.yaml.text:
1. Two players with a recorder. Swap sides between games (10, section 8).
2. Minimum: 4 games of A, 4 of B, 4 of C.
3. Fill the logging sheet (section 4) for every game.
4. Do not tune toward the historical result. Keep unexpected results in the log (Claude 03; Sol 16).

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 3: full campaign
rules.yaml.text:
1. At least 4 full campaigns with sides swapped.
2. Record the first round in which a faction qualifies. A win before the C3 Propaganda round in more than one game in five suggests thresholds are too low (10, section 8).
3. Check that each mandatory card's Always line fires once and only once (10, section 8).
4. Apply the DD-02 passivity measure (02, section 5.1) to every C3 to C5 Propaganda round.

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 4: optional modules
rules.yaml.text:
1. MOD-3B in C3 to C5 only, with the same card sequences as Stage 2 and 3 (section 8).
2. MOD-4A only after MOD-3B passes (02, section 6, step 6). Tests in 13, section B.5.
3. Concept B map last. Play the same eight-card sequence on both maps (13, section C.5).
4. Change one thing per test (13, rule for all parts).

rules.yaml.heading: Stage 5: outside readers
rules.yaml.text:
1. Invite readers with knowledge of modern Turkey, Kurdish politics or conflict studies, then readers with relevant civilian perspectives (Claude 03, Stage 3; Sol 16). These are recommended reviewers, not people who have agreed to take part.
2. Review T2 and T3 cards. This stage does not start until an opt-out rule for T2 cards and a survivor-aware review plan exist (Claude 03).

rules.yaml.heading: CT initiative versus the alternative
rules.yaml.text:
The CT lessons file calls the initiative system the largest revision. It asks for a test that isolates initiative.

| Item | Arm A (core) | Arm B (comparator) |
|---|---|---|
| Rule | CT track (M-029; 05, section 2) | Sol ranked choice (M-045; Sol 15, "Original test initiative procedure"): Pass below Limited below Event below Full, the smaller choice goes first, equal choices reverse, Pass +1 |
| Everything else | Same setup, deck seed, card order, costs and scoring | Same |

Procedure:

1. Use Scenario A in Stage 0. Play each deck seed once in each arm. Minimum 3 seeds.
2. Change nothing else between arms. Do not change combat, costs or victory in the same test (CT lessons).
3. Record for each arm: longest First Eligible streak, Pass share per faction, number of cards where a player had only one sensible choice and rules questions about eligibility.
4. Run the two-reader matrix check on Arm A (05, section 10).
5. Watch items for Arm A: the Event row and the Pass row of the responder matrix are design choices (05, section 2.3; DD-17). Log every use of those rows and any dispute.
6. Check the Pass contradiction in Arm B: count cards where a pass won priority.

Decision rule:

1. Keep Arm A if it has no streak over 4 cards in more than one game in three and readers agree on the matrix.
2. Switch to Arm B only if Arm A fails both checks and Arm B passes them. Record the change in the decisions file first (DD-04).
3. If both fail, revise the Event and Pass rows of Arm A before any other change.

rules.yaml.heading: Adversarial strategies
rules.yaml.text:
Play each one at least once in Stage 0 or Stage 1 (Sol 16):

1. State: force concentration with no Civic Action; Civic Action with minimal security; repeated Emergency Rule steps; Village Clearance at every legal chance.
2. PKK: sanctuary stacking; perpetual concealment; Coerce-only; ceasefire cycling.
3. Legal Politics (B and C): State closure at every chance.
4. MOD-3B: permanent alignment with each armed player; a continuity-only strategy.

For each exploit, decide whether it is numerical (tune it) or representational (redesign it), for example a rule that lets the PKK command a legal party (Sol 16).

rules.yaml.heading: MOD-3B promotion criteria
rules.yaml.text:
Run the module only in C3 to C5 (13, section A.1): at least 10 games, as test 3 needs, with the same card sequences as the core games it is compared with.

Promote MOD-3B to the default for C3 to C5 only if all three hold (02, section 5.1):

1. Core games show Legal Politics is passive: in more than half of recorded C3 to C5 Propaganda rounds, neither player changed a decision because of Legal Space or Offices.
2. In most debriefs, legal politics is named as the actor shown only as an automatic reaction.
3. The module passes its own tests (13, section A.9):

| # | Test | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Distinct legal options per turn | Mean of 4 or more |
| 2 | Special activity use | Op + SA in at least one third of Legal Movement 1st or 2nd Eligible actions |
| 3 | Own win path | Top margin in at least 2 of 10 games, with a positive PKK margin in at least one |
| 4 | Kingmaker | Fewer than 1 in 4 games where it has no path to win and its later actions change the State and PKK order |
| 5 | Neutrality on C-025 | No State or PKK strategy depends on Legal Movement pieces as its own asset |
| 6 | Load | C3 to C5 play time rises by no more than 25 percent [tune] |
| 7 | Core comparison | The same card sequence in core mode fails the passivity test |

Retire the module and keep the core (02, section 5.2) if tests 1, 3 or 5 fail, if it becomes a routine kingmaker or if a source set shows the legal parties acted as PKK organs.

rules.yaml.heading: Stop rules
rules.yaml.text:
Stop play and fix before the next game when:

1. A missing procedure needs a table ruling. Write the decision first (Sol 16).
2. The same rules error occurs three times. Rewrite the rule (Claude 03).
3. Any harmful action shows a positive net score change for its user. Stop all tests until fixed (M-028; 09, section 7).
4. A faction wins with a Harm count above its limit. Treat it as a rules error.
5. A tester reports distress with a card. Mark the card, review its tier and take it to Stage 5 readers (Claude 03).
6. A player has no useful action on three cards in a row more than once per game (Sol 16).
7. Scores cannot be reproduced by a second reader (Sol 16).
8. An exploit found in section 7 wins two games in a row.

Win-rate screen: with two players the chance rate is 50 percent. Flag a side for review if it wins 8 or more of 10 games across swapped seats. This is a screen for a severe problem only. It is not a balance test, and the Claude 60 percent rule for three seats is not used (Sol 16).

rules.yaml.heading: Materials
rules.yaml.text:
1. Draft map, generic counters and tracks for the DD-05 map (03; 04).
2. Piles C1 to C5 built under 05, section 1.1. The event chapter (08) is not yet written. Until it exists, use the mandatory structural cards (10, section 6.1) plus clearly labeled fictional neutral prompts. Fictional prompts never count toward the supported-card target (Sol 16).
3. One-page play aid (05, section 8) with the full responder matrix.
4. Logging sheet (section 4) and outcome record sheet (09, section 6).

rules.yaml.heading: Exit criteria and audit trail
rules.yaml.text:
The prototype phase ends when:

1. Section 5 questions pass in at least two thirds of the games where they are live.
2. No unresolved ethics issue remains.
3. The initiative decision (section 6) and the MOD-3B decision (section 8) are recorded in the decisions file.

Each test version records which source-based constraint changed, which value changed and why. Factual corrections go to the historical register. Balance changes go to the design log. A mechanical change must not rewrite the history to justify itself (Sol 16).
